key_insight: Low-dimensional perovskite capping increases surface roughness while preserving electronic uniformity and suppressing aging-induced optoelectronic disorder.
engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a route toward durable perovskite photovoltaics without requiring smoother surfaces as a proxy for electronic quality.
method: Cap 3D perovskites with Ruddlesden–Popper layers derived from 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium.
Combine statistical AFM with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare morphology, emission, and quasi-Fermi level splitting before and after accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films show enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more spatially uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting than pristine films, including after accelerated aging.
watch_item: The abstract does not report device efficiency or operational lifetime, so photovoltaic performance gains remain to be established.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
